title: service-boundary-enforcer-and-declarative-kms-mapper
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: customers with strict regulatory envelopes asked for stronger guarantees that KMS usage and RBAC decisions respect declared service boundaries (e.g. datasets, operator roles, and tenant pinning) while keeping the policy model declarative and auditable. This PR implements a service-boundary enforcer that validates request-scoped claims against a declarative KMS-binding policy and routes audit events through a shard-aware audit sink. The change is split into three logical pieces: 1) policy/decl-mapper: a compact DSL and evaluation engine to map service/tenant attributes to allowed KMS provider bindings (supports multiple providers, per-tenant allowlists, and temporary operator overrides), 2) runtime/enforcer: a lightweight middleware that performs enforcement at the request edge, emits canonical audit markers, and short-circuits unsafe KMS calls with a clear error and remediation hints, and 3) observability/audit-router: a configurable router that shards audit events by jurisdiction and retention class to separate sinks (S3/BigQuery/GCS) and attaches signed provenance headers. Checklist: - [x] DSL spec and examples - [x] Decl-mapper implementation + unit tests - [x] Enforcer middleware and integration tests - [x] Audit router with sink adapters and provenance headers - [x] Helm chart changes for private installers - [x] Documentation and upgrade notes Backwards compatibility: The DSL defaults are permissive for existing deployments; operators must opt-in to stricter enforcement in the Console or via the new ConfigMap. Rollout plan: staged enablement by tenant cohort using a rollout flag and safe-fallback to previous KMS behavior when policy evaluation fails (fail-open for non-enforced tenants; fail-closed optional per organization). Related work: ENG-3456 (service-boundary policy), SEC-112 (audit provenance), PM-789 (compliance rollouts).

release_notes: Adds a declarative service-boundary policy DSL and runtime enforcer that can be opted into per-tenant; introduces audit-sink sharding for region-aware retention. No immediate breaking changes; operators must enable enforcement explicitly. See docs/security/service-boundary.md for migration steps.
discussion_summary: Initial reviewers requested stricter error codes and clearer remediation text when a request is blocked. Diego asked for a performance microbenchmark; we added a small load test showing ~1% p99 overhead in the edge path. Priya requested an extra integration test covering operator-scope override TTLs, which was added. A transient flaky test in CI caused one rerun; after the rerun all checks passed. Final sign-off granted by Samir (security lead).
ci_checks: integration-tests: pass (rerun once - flaky db test)
notes_for_ops: Operators should review the example policy files in policy/decl-mapper/README.md and enable enforcement via the Console feature flag or the helm value 'security.serviceBoundary.enforce=true'. When enabling for the first time, run the migration script tests/integration/kms_binding_residency_test.go against a staging cluster to confirm KMS provider mappings. Audit router requires credentials for configured sinks and an HSM/KMS key for signing provenance headers; fallback to unsigned mode is available but not recommended.
security_impact: Medium: introduces enforcement logic that, if misconfigured, could block KMS operations. Mitigations: default to opt-in, fail-open behavior for unmanaged tenants, clear audit trails and allowlist mechanisms for emergency bypass.
upgrade_instructions: 1) Install helm chart changes with values.yaml updated; 2) Deploy enforcer in canary mode for a small tenant cohort; 3) Verify audit sink delivery and provenance headers; 4) Gradually flip enforcement flag per cohort; 5) If a tenant is blocked, use the Console's temporary operator override or update the declarative policy and redeploy
example_policy_snippet:
- service: model-serving
  tenants: [acct-123, acct-789]
  allowed_kms: [aws:us-east-1:kms/alias/redwood, gcp:projects/prod/locations/global/keyRings/kr/cryptoKeys/ck]
  operator_overrides_ttl: 3600s
why_this_is_unique: Unlike previous PRs that focused solely on region pinning or KMS provenance, this change ties a small declarative policy language directly into the runtime enforcement path and pairs it with audit sharding. The DSL is intentionally compact to make audits and reviews easier for compliance teams.
